ety.text: From on- + set. Compare Old English onsettan (“to impose; oppress, bear down”). For semantic parallels for the meaning to assault, compare cognate Russian насе́сть pf (naséstʹ), наседа́ть impf (nasedátʹ).

senses.d: The initial phase of a disease or condition, in which symptoms first become apparent.
The initial portion of a syllable, preceding the syllable nucleus.
The beginning of a musical note or other sound, in which the amplitude rises from zero to an initial peak.

ex: There is surely no greater wisdom than well to time the beginnings and onsets of things.

senses.d: Anything added, such as an ornament or as a useful appendage.
An attack; an assault especially of an army.
ex:
Heralds, from off our towers, we might behold
From first to last, the onset and retire
Of both your armies
Who on that day the word of onset gave.

grp.label: (medicine) initial phase of a disease or condition
